value.overview: The Herring Gull (Larus argentatus) is a gull recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from large gull size, pale gray mantle, white head in breeding adults, pink legs, and red spot on the lower bill. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 42 state or DC summaries, including AK, AL, CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, GA, IA, ID, IL, IN, KS, KY, and 28 more. It is most associated with Coasts:  Beach and Estuary and Wetlands:  Lakes and Rivers, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Herring Gull belongs to the family Gulls, Terns, and Skimmers in the order Charadriiformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for large gull size, pale gray mantle, white head in breeding adults, pink legs, and red spot on the lower bill. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
